title: Cash in Lieu of Replacement under Homeowner Service Contracts
content:
Cash in lieu is the settlement by which Bridgewell pays cash in place of providing a replacement unit under a Homeowner Service Contract.

**1. Company-elected offers.** Bridgewell offers cash in lieu, with the settlement basis "company elected", instead of providing a replacement when a replacement is warranted under the repair-or-replace standard but a like unit cannot be sourced or installed through the network.

**2. Customer-elected cash.** A customer who holds a replacement authorization that is not yet completed may ask for cash instead, with the settlement basis "customer elected".

**3. Offer amount — retired in part.**
> The offer amount is Bridgewell's contracted replacement cost for the like unit, limited to the remaining item benefit and the remaining aggregate benefit (for a customer-elected offer, computed as if the replacement authorization it replaces had already been reversed), and rounded to the cent; supplemental allowances and service call fees are never added.

This sentence is **no longer in force** for a customer-elected settlement, nor for a company-elected offer on a standing replacement authorization that no network contractor can install; each of those is worked out under the current rule for it. For every other offer it remains the rule.

**4. Offer expiry.** The offer expiration date is the tier's offer validity (calendar days) after the offer date.

**5. Acceptance window — retired in part.**
> Cash in lieu is paid only when the customer accepts an offer on file no later than the offer validity's calendar days after the offer is issued; the count starts the day after the offer date and the boundary day itself qualifies.

This sentence is **no longer in force** for a customer-elected settlement, which is governed by the current rule for it; every company-elected settlement remains under this offer-and-acceptance rule. *Boundary pair, hypothetical, 30-day validity, offer issued March 1:* acceptance on March 31 (day 30, the expiration date) is in time; acceptance on April 1 is not.

**6. Acceptance and payment.** Accepting is the customer's own decision and is recorded by the customer.
> The payment equals the accepted offer amount and carries the offer's settlement basis

— this part is **no longer in force** for a customer-elected settlement and for the acceptance of a company-elected offer made because no network contractor can install the replacement; each is paid under the current rule for it. For every other accepted offer it remains the rule. A customer-elected payment names the replacement authorization it replaces, which is reversed in full the same day. Payment is issued within the tier's cash-in-lieu payment window (calendar days) after acceptance.

**7. Expired offers.** An expired offer cannot be accepted, and the agent may issue a new offer at the then-current contracted replacement cost.

**8. Once per request.** Cash in lieu is paid at most once per service request. Once cash in lieu is paid on a request, no repair or replacement is authorized on it.

| Fact on the request | Effect |
|---|---|
| Cash in lieu already paid on the request | no second cash payment; no repair or replacement authorization |
| Company-elected offer past its expiration date | cannot be accepted; a new offer may be issued at the then-current contracted replacement cost |
